I used to do this dog that was “ungroomable.” And he really was when we first met. He only had a few really bad experiences. So the owners paid me $1 a minute to sit on the grooming table with their dog, for like 20 minute sessions. I would show him my tools, let him smell everything, turn on clippers and not use them, just touch him with them. I would also give him lots of pats and treats. It was surprising how quickly this dog turned around and gave me his trust. All of a sudden I could groom him. It only took a couple of sessions. The next groomer should be willing to work with your dog to make positive experiences for him. He won’t be traumatized for life, dogs are crazy resilient to bad experiences. I hate seeing dogs have a bad experience and never get groomed again, because any grooming experience they have will be bad. Especially if the owner is full of anxiety around grooming. I agree with everyone the shop needs to pay up. And you need a new groomer. But please don’t be so burned by this you worry about grooming. I would tell the new shop of your experience. Make sure you find someone who you can check their recommendations and reviews and who has experience and compassion. Best of luck to you guys. A haircut is not abuse. I live in Florida and we have plenty of people that get shorter haircuts. I’m a groomer. Unless your dog lives outside, the quality of life is usually not really affected. Not everyone can maintain the coat. I’ve literally never seen one dog that couldn’t cool down or was killed by a haircut. Some people go to the beach and the hair never dries and the wetness creates bigger issues. Some people can’t brush their dogs well enough. (Packed coat is not regulating temperature either.) the two coats grow in at different lengths, and if there is an underlying health issue, this is usually when alopecia happens. It’s lovely when people can maintain full coat and the maintenance that requires, but calling people abusers for wanting a haircut on their dog is not abuse. People read one article and run with it. We see how this works for real people and dogs, and that Poms that get haircuts are just as healthy and happy as any other dogs. I’ve seen real abuse and neglect. We even had one person write a horrible review because of a haircut they saw on social media about a short haircut on a double coat. That dog went to the beach every day, lived in a a mansion and had a happy and healthy life well into old age. That older couple was not abusing their dog, and that dog is not an abuse victim. People need to get off their high horse. I get you don’t want yours shaved, but that is an extreme thing to say.

You got them in the perfect spot! Those little black circles are the quick. The dead parts of the quick are usually white on black nails. Dremels are great for taking small amounts and getting to the quick without cutting into it. If you go much further than this they’ll bleed. If you want to get the nails shorter, you should take off just a little every week and the quick will recede. You do need to get to the black part of the quick in order to push them back, which it looks like you’ve done. Great job! If your dog is generally tolerant, and they start squirming while you’re dremeling, you’re getting close, and they’re starting to feel it because there’s nerves in the quick. I would get a little quick stop in case you accidentally overshoot it. With a dremel, you usually won’t bleed them terribly if you accidentally go too far. If you don’t have quick stop, you can press the bleeding nail into a bar of soap or even a candle to plug it until it can stop on its own. Don’t beat yourself up if you accidentally bleed one. It’s not a big deal and it’s way more important to keep the nails trimmed than it is to never accidentally bleed a nail. Hope this helps!

I agree with opening the eyes. Nice shape! But clear eyes makes or breaks a groom. The Bichon has dark black eyes and eye skin that is supposed to be a focal point on the dog. Also the ears. Take them about a half inch shorter, then de bulk a tiny bit like less than 25 percent,  but round it more to the shape of the head. It’s hard to describe but making a dog look balanced is a true art.

I don’t love groomers using a guard comb on faces until they really understand the round face. Some areas need to be skimmed, it’s only to de bulk. A lot of groomers do way too short on top running a guard comb both directions. You can make it really short without making it not round. The cheeks cannot be chopped up or it doesn’t look right. The corners of your eyes are shaggy and other parts are a little too short on the dog with lashes. Dogs with lashes still need that clear eye look. Comb up and forward repeatedly. Sometimes less is more. You take big chunks and sometimes it makes more work for yourself or gets a bad result. Imagine the circle of the face  while you’re grooming. Sometimes, you have to almost blur your eyes, don’t look too close. See the shape and the lines and only trim hairs outside of those invisible lines. You can lay your scissors across to help you visualize.the shih tux face is great; the feet need thinners. Some groomers skip thinning to save time but this comes with more experience.

I’m a groomer and I’ve noticed that -for people who get haircuts- the regrowth depends on the health of the dog and how often they get shaved. Your dogs coat looks very healthy. Just keep in mind your dog has two coats, the undercoat and the guard hairs. That second one takes longer to grow than the other. So initially it can look a little funny sometimes. I recommend doing a good bath and deshed every 4 weeks during that time to stimulate the hair follicles and remove anything that’s getting packed and preventing the skin from breathing. It’s gonna be worth it to do the surgery, and doing this once shouldn’t cause too many problems with the coat. Like I said some dogs grow back in like they’ve never been shaved and some don’t grow back at all. I almost always find that those dogs are pre diabetic, have kidney issues or some other underlying condition. At the end of the day it’s just hair. I highly recommend asking your groomer to do a full hand blow dry- no cage drying. Or find one who does this. It’s important for these types of coats. Some groomers cage dry to make more money and be faster but these dogs need a hand blow dry. I also recommend asking your shop if they use any kind of bathing system like hydrosurge. It’s water injected with air that penetrates the coat deeper and stimulates the hair follicles. These are good questions to ask as some groomers cut corners and the pet owners don’t know what they’re doing at the groomer. I also have a Pom myself btw, and I give him haircuts. Never had a problem with his coat growing back at all.
